article.title: NFL EDGE Thursday Evening Brief
article.dek: The inactive list settled Thursday's two game-time calls, the board still has not flipped to Week 9, and Sunday already has a quarterback change worth knowing about.

items.headline: Lead: Inactives are in — Tuten and Walker play, Wiggins is out
paragraphs: Kickoff is 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video, and the last unknowns are settled. Jacksonville running back Bhayshul Tuten is active after missing all week with ankle and foot injuries. He worked out before the game and is good to go. Defensive end Travon Walker is active too, after being questionable with a rib injury.

Baltimore is without its top cornerback. Nate Wiggins is inactive with a stinger and an illness. He was a full participant Tuesday, then missed Wednesday's practice. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins misses a third straight game with a knee injury.

The quarterback picture is unchanged and now final. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano makes his first career start. Austin Reed, signed Monday, is the backup. Kedon Slovis is the emergency third quarterback. The Brissett trade is still a next-week story, not a Thursday one.
items.takeaway: Tuten and Walker play for Jacksonville; Wiggins is out for Baltimore, and Fagnano starts with Reed backing him up.

items.headline: Sunday quarterback news: Darnold is out, Lock starts for Seattle
paragraphs: Seattle will be without starting quarterback Sam Darnold on Sunday against Arizona. Darnold is out with a quad injury suffered late in Monday's loss to Chicago. He will not go on injured reserve, and the team calls him week-to-week, but he is out for Week 9.

Drew Lock starts in his place. Lock has been dealing with an elbow injury of his own and was limited in practice for two weeks, so Seattle plans to manage his throwing workload and give Jalen Milroe practice reps. The Seahawks added quarterback Adrian Martinez to the practice squad on Wednesday for depth.

In Philadelphia, Joe Milton will start at quarterback Sunday against the Giants. Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots. Tanner McKee, who has a chest injury but was a full participant, moves to the backup role.
items.takeaway: Darnold is out Sunday and Lock starts with a sore elbow; in Philadelphia, Milton starts with McKee backing him up.

items.headline: Weather: scattered thunderstorms possible at kickoff in Baltimore
paragraphs: Thursday night in Baltimore looks wet at kickoff. The forecast for M&T Bank Stadium calls for scattered thunderstorms around 8:00 p.m. ET, about 70 degrees, with a rain chance near 43 percent at kickoff and 49 percent at 9:00 p.m. Wind is light, out of the south-southwest at about 5 miles per hour.

That is a factual weather read, not a totals edge. Rain chances stay in the picture through the evening, with showers possible again late. If you are going, pack for rain. If you are betting, do not turn a rain chance into a totals opinion on its own.
items.takeaway: About 70 degrees at kickoff in Baltimore, light south wind, and scattered thunderstorms possible during the game.

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — no Week 9 cards, so Thursday still goes through Check
paragraphs: Read after the evening refresh window and checked again a few minutes later, the app board still shows Week 8, generated November 2. There are no Week 9 cards at all. Its Baltimore game is still the Week 8 trip to Buffalo, and its quarterback field is blank — it has not picked up Fagnano as tonight's starter.

So there is still no Thursday card to read, and you should not force a pick out of a stale board. That is what Check is for. If your book has a Thursday line, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

The only cards on the board are Monday's Chicago at Seattle game, which has already been played. They are worth one look because they show how the three cards differ. The Value card and the Balanced card were the same play: Chicago +3 at -102, with the model giving Chicago a 50.6% chance against a market price implying 46.5% — a +3.6% edge. The Hit Rate card was Seattle on the moneyline at -175, with the model at 56.1% against a market price implying 60.4%. Hit Rate is the pick the app thinks is most likely to win. It is not the best value. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
items.takeaway: Board still shows Week 8 with no Week 9 cards, so Thursday's price goes through Check until the board flips.

items.headline: Learn the Game: handle vs. tickets — money and bets are not the same thing
paragraphs: When a betting splits page shows two percentages, they are counting different things. Handle is the money. Tickets are the bets. A side can have most of the tickets and a minority of the handle, or the other way around.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say 70% of the tickets are on the favorite, but only 40% of the handle is. That means lots of small bets on the favorite and fewer, bigger bets on the underdog. The crowd is on one side. The money is split differently.

Why it matters: a real Fade starts from a disagreement like that — heavy tickets on one side, handle leaning the other — plus a line move that backs it up. Tickets and handle agreeing on the same side is not a Fade. It is just a popular side.
items.takeaway: Handle is the money, tickets are the bets — when they point opposite ways, that disagreement is where a Fade starts.

items.headline: Thursday's line ticked to Jacksonville -10, and the total held at 39.5
paragraphs: The Thursday line moved a half-point through the day and the total did not move at all. At DraftKings, Jacksonville is now -10 at -108, with Baltimore +10 at -112. The moneyline is Jacksonville -535 and Baltimore +400. The total is 39.5, over -118 and under -102.

Step back and the move is still the quarterback news. A week ago the lookahead had Baltimore as a 3-point favorite with a total of 48.5. Jackson's thumb injury, Huntley's season-ending turf toe, and Fagnano's first start flipped the favorite and pulled the total down about nine points. The market has now settled around Jacksonville by 10 with a total near 40.

Sunday has its own mover already. Seattle was -11.5 against Arizona on Wednesday, and by Thursday morning it was -8.5. That is the Darnold news landing in the number. Watch Friday's final designations before you act on a Sunday price — the inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff.

The app has not caught any of it yet. The board still shows Week 8, generated November 2, so none of these prices are on a card. If your book has a line you like, run it through Check: type in the line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator for a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Jacksonville -10 at DraftKings with the total steady at 39.5; Seattle's Sunday line has already moved three points on the Darnold news.

items.headline: Thursday game? Thursday check — and bet the good number now
paragraphs: The inactives are settled, so there is nothing left to wait on for tonight. If your book has a Thursday number you like, run it through Check now and, if Check says bet, bet it now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number later, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too. And a quick price reminder: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and how aggressive you want to be.
For Sunday, the next real information event is Friday's final designations. That is the one to wait for on a Sunday price — not tonight's game, which is already priced and about to kick off.
items.takeaway: Inactives are in, so run your book's Thursday price through Check now; if it says bet, bet the good number now.
